description: One skew-Hadamard matrix for each order from 4 to 1200 that is not open in baselines/hadamard-orders.json and that the board does not hold as a verified quadruple; for the orders the board holds, the site derives the matrix from an entry. After these come found matrices of orders above 1200, which the orders file and the grid do not cover. Each record gives the order, the file, the sha256 of the uncompressed text, the construction and its parameters, the keys of the sources in baselines/references.bib, the origin of the file and how it was generated. A file is the matrix as text, one row per line, + for 1 and - for -1, compressed with xz. For a doubled order the sources are those of the doubling construction followed by those of the matrix that is doubled, and the doubling of H is the block matrix with rows (H, H) and (-H^T, H^T). The files of origin sagemath were generated on 2026-11-24 with passagemath-combinat 10.8.14, a modular distribution of SageMath, on CPython 3.12 by the call skew_hadamard_matrix(n, check=False, skew_normalize=False) after set_random_seed(n), followed by the skew normalisation D M D with D the diagonal matrix of the first row of M; the function named in a record is the builder that call reached. The files of origin repository come from the software repository cited as kishan2026skew, which is not peer reviewed. The files of origin board are doublings of the Goethals-Seidel array of the named board entry, with its skew block first and in the block layout of site/skew.py; a test rebuilds them from the entry. A matrix of origin found is one found by a search run for this board that is not a board quadruple: its record gives the date, the contributors, the array (williamson8 for the 8-Williamson array, bordered for the bordered array of Wallis and Whiteman, bordered8 for the bordered eight-block array), the rows, the multiplier that fixes every row, the row sums, the search and the checks made before it was stored. A williamson8 record has eight rows of one length and the sign of each block. A bordered record has the moduli of the group Z_m1 x ... x Z_mk and four rows indexed by its elements in lexicographic order, the last component fastest; its multiplier acts componentwise. A bordered record may have a pairing, a multiplier that carries the first row to the third and the second to the fourth and that applied twice is z -> z or z -> -z; the build checks it. A bordered8 record is for the bordered eight-block array, which we did not find in the sources we read: it has eight rows of one length, the first of skew type and the others symmetric, and a sentence on how the array was derived. The build rebuilds a found matrix from the rows with site/skew.py and compares it with the file. A found matrix of an order above 1200 has no file: its sha256 is that of the rebuilt text, one row per line as in a file, and the build compares it and runs the same exact check. The files of origin sagemath and repository were not produced by this repository's code. The site build decompresses each file, compares its sha256 with the one recorded here, and checks exactly that the matrix H of order n has entries 1 and -1 and satisfies H H^T = nI and H + H^T = 2I. A note says where a source that a construction goes back to is not cited.

matrices.search: The search fixes the multiplier 36 and takes every row of length 101 that is constant on its orbits: 1,024 rows of skew type and 1,024 symmetric rows of positive row sum, among which 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 19, 21 are the only seven row sums whose squares add to 807. It joins three symmetric rows against the skew row and the other four through a 64-bit hash of the summed periodic autocorrelations and rechecks every match in integers; the run stopped with 11 solutions after about 7.9 million of the 1.4 × 10¹² combinations on the larger side, and this matrix is the first of them, so the search is not a census.
matrices.checked: Before it was stored, the file was also checked by two programs that share no code with the build: one builds the matrix from the rows by index arithmetic and compares its rows as Python integers, and the other checks the two defining conditions with integer numpy arrays.

A search of the sources named in this note on 2026-11-25 found no earlier skew-Hadamard matrix of order 808; this reports the search and does not claim priority. The sources checked were the SageMath list of orders with no known skew-Hadamard matrix [@sage2026unknown], the preprints [@cati2024database], [@egan2026recent] and [@djokovic2023skew], and the skew directory of the repository [@kishan2026skew]. Sources read on 2026-11-26 agree: the table in [@seberry1992hadamard] of the least t for which a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 2ᵗq is known gives t = 10 for q = 101; the census [@djokovic2025census] lists v = 101 among the 737 odd v below 2500 for which a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 4v is undecided, and does not cover orders 8v or 16v; and the note [@kumar2026skew] constructs skew-Hadamard matrices of order 4v for 106 of those v, of order 2ᵗv with t = 3 or 4 for twelve odd v, and of order 3(q + 1) for every prime power q congruent to 3 modulo 4, none of them of order 808.

It joins the row of skew type and one other row against the remaining two through a 64-bit hash of the summed periodic autocorrelations and rechecks every match in integers. Its output holds 4 solutions, and this matrix is the first of them. How many rows the run drew, its seed and its running time were not recorded, so the search is not a census.

matrices.note: The result has not been reviewed. A search of the sources named in this note on 2026-11-25 found no earlier skew-Hadamard matrix of order 1416; this reports the search and does not claim priority. The sources checked were the table in [@cati2024database] of the least t for which a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 2ᵗm is known, which gives t = 4 for m = 177, while 1416 = 2³ × 177; the survey [@egan2026recent]; and the skew directory of the repository [@kishan2026skew]. The table in [@cati2024database] is the reference we compared against, not a guarantee that no smaller order is known. Sources read on 2026-11-26 agree: the table in [@seberry1992hadamard] of the least t for which a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 2ᵗq is known marks q = 177 as having no such order known for any t; the census [@djokovic2025census] lists v = 177 among the 737 odd v below 2500 for which a skew-Hadamard matrix of order 4v is undecided, and does not cover orders 8v or 16v; and the note [@kumar2026skew] constructs skew-Hadamard matrices of order 4v for 106 of those v, of order 2ᵗv with t = 3 or 4 for twelve odd v, and of order 3(q + 1) for every prime power q congruent to 3 modulo 4, none of them of order 1416. Other tables of skew-Hadamard orders in books were not read. The infinite families we know of were checked by arithmetic and none gives order 1416: the constructions from a prime power q need 1416 − 1, 1416/2 − 1 or 1416/4 − 1 to be a prime power of a suitable form, and 1415 = 5 × 283 and 707 = 7 × 101 are not prime powers, and 353 is a prime congruent to 33 modulo 64, for which the finite-field families of [@momihara2019constructions] have sixteen blocks and no array is given; and a product of a smaller skew-Hadamard matrix with an amicable pair would need an order that is itself not known. The other families in the list of skew-Hadamard orders in [@seberry1992hadamard] were tested by arithmetic on 2026-11-26: (p − 1)ᵘ + 1 for p the order of a skew-Hadamard matrix and u odd, (|t| + 1)(q + 1) for a prime power q = s² + 4t² congruent to 5 modulo 8, 4(q² + q + 1) for a prime power q [@spence1975skew], and mn(n − 1) from orthogonal designs [@seberry1978skew]. The first three do not give order 1416. The last has the shape of 1416 with n = 4 and m = 118, and of 708 with n = 4 and m = 59: it would give these orders from an orthogonal design OD(472; 1, 118, 353), or OD(236; 1, 59, 176) for 708, and we know of no source for such a design. The family 3(q + 1) of [@kumar2026skew] and the other closed-form families we tested do not give order 1416 either. This check covers the families named in the sources above and is not a proof that no published construction applies.
